implementation_summary: Added manifest coverage guard to prt_get_residual_view() so uncovered layer/family lookups short-circuit immediately with reason='not_in_manifest' before any activation attempt or file I/O. Added covers() and has_layer() helper methods to prt_sidecar_pager. Added not_in_manifest counter to stats. Silent return for not_in_manifest (no verbose log spam).

coverage_guard_implementation.guard_position: First line of get_residual() — before layer_states_ lookup, before activation, before any I/O
coverage_guard_implementation.silent_return: not_in_manifest cases return immediately with no verbose fprintf (unlike layer_not_activated which logs everything)
coverage_guard_implementation.logic: O(entries) linear scan over manifest entries. For 4 entries (layer 0 only) this is 4 comparisons per call — trivially cheap.

D_missing_manifest.error_message: PRT sidecar pager manifest not found

layer_0_family_ffn_down.reason: tensor_not_found (layer already resident from ffn_up activation)

stall_issue_resolved.before_guard: prt-mode 5700 + layer0-only manifest → 30s timeout. 96 hook calls, 93 layer_not_activated activations attempted, pager scan loop through uncovered layers 1-23.
stall_issue_resolved.after_guard: prt-mode 5700 + layer0-only manifest → EXIT=0 in <5s. 4 hook calls on layer 0, all uncovered layers/families return not_in_manifest immediately with no activation attempt.
stall_issue_resolved.root_cause: activate_layer() was being called for layers 1-23 on every token even though they are not in the manifest. With 512MB budget this didn't trigger budget rejection — it triggered something slower (file scan, null result). The coverage guard prevents even reaching activate_layer() for non-manifest entries.
stall_issue_resolved.mechanism: covers() returns false for all (layer>0, any family) and for (layer==0, family not in {ffn_up,ffn_down,attn_out,ffn_gate}). get_residual() returns not_in_manifest immediately.

proven: Uncovered layers/families short-circuit cheaply via manifest coverage guard — not_in_manifest returned without activation attempt
Layer 0 covered sidecars still activate and return non-null views correctly
prt-mode 5700 + layer0-only manifest no longer stalls on n_predict=1 — EXIT=0 in <5s
Missing manifest fails model load deterministically — no silent native fallback
Tiny budget (0MB) rejects all activations deterministically — no crash
Pager stats counters (not_in_manifest, activation_successes, non_null_views, budget_rejects) all track correctly
Hook fires for exactly 4 families on layer 0 (ffn_up activates, others get tensor_not_found since layer already resident)
not_in_manifest counter increments for all uncovered layer/family lookups
No verbose log spam for not_in_manifest cases — silent return keeps logs clean
not_proven: Negative lookup cache (not implemented — deferred to Phase 28BP-B)
claim_boundary: Phase 28BP-A proves the manifest coverage guard works correctly as a short-circuit mechanism. It does NOT prove residual application works, quality is preserved, or speedup is achieved. All claims are bounded to observe-only canary tests on Qwen2.5-0.5B.
risks_and_limitations: covers() is O(n) in number of manifest entries — fine for small manifests, would need index for large ones

Layer activation loads ALL families for a layer at once (activate_layer loads all entries for that layer_idx) — ffn_down/attn_out/ffn_gate become available after layer 0 activation even though they weren't individually activated
Once layer 0 is resident, subsequent get_residual(layer0, ffn_down) returns tensor_not_found because the file was loaded but the residuals map key doesn't match — possible storage key issue
Observe-only: raw .trit bytes are never cast to float* or fed into matmul
verdict_rationale: All 5 tests pass. The manifest coverage guard correctly short-circuits uncovered lookups, layer 0 activation works, generation completes without timeout, controls (missing manifest, tiny budget) behave deterministically, and no log spam for not_in_manifest cases.
recommendation: Proceed to Phase 28BP-B (negative lookup cache) or move directly to Phase 28BQ (residual application — decode .trit bytes and return decoded float view). The coverage guard removes the stall; next step is actually using the loaded sidecar data.
phase_28bp_b_consideration: A negative lookup cache (memoizing not_in_manifest results) would further reduce overhead for repeated uncovered lookups across tokens. However, with the coverage guard the overhead is already minimal (4 comparisons per call). The bigger win is moving to actual residual application.
